explanations: luna: The source reads dīn in 95:7 as a settled religious way while the whole surah's closing judgment question also leaves the judgment sense in view. This ayah names God “مَٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ,” making that reckoning sense explicit.
luna: The worshippers ask God to guide them to the straight path. This is a direct devotional formulation of the upright course named in the source.

luna: The people addressed say they are only reformers while being told not to cause corruption; 2:12 answers that they are the corrupters, though unaware. This concretely activates the source's definition of ṣalāḥ as the opposite of fasād in deeds. | terra: When told not to spread corruption, the offenders claim إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ, posing the exact ṣalāḥ/fasād opposition as a dispute about conduct.

luna: This ayah exposes the contradiction in 2:11: the people who claim to reform are in fact corrupters. It supplies the negative side of the source's ṣ-l-ḥ / fasād distinction. | terra: God identifies those professed reformers as the actual corrupters, supplying the judgment missing from their self-description.
terra: The command to worship “your Lord who created you” makes human creation itself the ground for obedience and taqwā.

terra: The source dictionary cites al-khalāq as “religion,” whereas مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ here means no allotted share in the Hereafter; the same form marks a necessary semantic boundary.

luna: The source explicitly names this verse for the root ر د د: some People of the Book wish to turn believers into disbelievers “مِّنۢ بَعْدِ إِيمَٰنِكُمْ.” Its own context makes the source's “after” link and reversal of faith explicit. | terra: لَوْ يَرُدُّونَكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمَانِكُمْ كُفَّارًا supplies the section's exact return-after-faith relation and makes the reversal an intended pressure from others.
terra: Submitting one's face to God while doing good yields secure reward; inward surrender, outward ṣalāḥ, orientation, and recompense align in one sentence.

luna: The ayah asks who would turn away from Abraham's way except someone who makes a foolish choice, then says God chose him. It supplies a concrete turning away from the hanīf course described in the source. | terra: Turning away from Abraham's milla is called self-stultification, while his election and righteousness state the fit between sound self and upright religion.
terra: Abraham answers the command “submit” with submission to the Lord of the worlds, enacting dīn as obedience.
terra: Abraham and Jacob charge their children to remain in the chosen dīn until death as submitters, making steadfastness a transmitted way of life.

luna: When challenged to become Jews or Christians to be guided, the answer is to follow Abraham's hanīf way. It is a direct repeated formulation of the upright Abrahamic religion named in the source. | terra: The answer to sectarian religious claims is Abraham's milla as a ḥanīf, a direct companion to 6:161's upright religion.
terra: God's “coloring” is claimed as unsurpassed while the speakers declare worship, a nonlexical image of divinely given formation expressed as religion.
terra: The test distinguishes one who follows the Messenger from one who يَنْقَلِبُ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ, staging religious reversal as turning back on the heels.

luna: The ayah says righteousness is not merely turning faces east or west, then describes faith, giving, prayer, covenant-keeping, and patience. It clarifies how the source's face-oriented religion becomes a whole pattern of righteous conduct. | terra: Righteousness is unfolded as belief, giving, prayer, alms, covenant-keeping, and patience, showing how inward faith becomes a stable pattern of صالح conduct.
terra: مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ again uses khalāq for an afterlife share, distinct from the source's cited dictionary sense “religion.”

luna: The person who turns away strives to spread corruption and destroy crops and offspring, and God does not love corruption. This puts the source's opposition between righteous deeds and corruption into a concrete pattern of action.

luna: The source explicitly cites this answer about fighting in the sacred month: opponents seek to turn believers from their religion, and whoever turns from it is named. It gives the exact religious-apostasy setting that the source's r-d-d dictionary note evokes. | terra: The ayah explicitly joins attempts to يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَنْ دِينِكُمْ with whoever يَرْتَدِدْ ... عَنْ دِينِهِ, the section's cited religious sense of the r-d-d family.

luna: In its discussion of orphans, the ayah says God knows the corrupter from the reformer. It directly activates the source's dictionary explanation of ṣalāḥ as the opposite of fasād in deeds. | terra: In conduct toward orphans, إِصْلَاحٌ is better and God knows الْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ, directly defining the action-level opposition named by the source.
terra: “Stand before God devoutly obedient” makes bodily standing a direct enactment of dīn as obedience.

luna: The source says religion and truth stand by their support; this ayah names God “ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ” and says neither sleep nor slumber overtakes Him. It presents God as the sustaining ground behind all that stands. | terra: الْقَيُّومُ names God as the self-subsisting sustainer, the ultimate q-w-m sense behind the section's idea of that by which created life and truth stand.
terra: Once right guidance is distinct from error, belief in God is grasping الْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَى; the unbreakable support makes the section's “religion by which one stands” visible.

luna: The ayah describes God as “قَائِمًا بِٱلْقِسْطِ” (upholding justice). This directly activates the source's ق و م branch connecting standing/uprightness with justice, and presents God as its ground. | terra: God is قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ, maintaining justice, and the next ayah names Islam as the dīn before Him; q-w-m and justice meet exactly as in the source definition.
terra: الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ identifies religion with submission immediately after God is described as standing in justice.
luna: Jesus says God is his Lord and theirs, commands worship of Him, and calls this the straight path. This joins the source's dīn-as-obedience sense to a direct formulation of the upright way.

luna: Abraham is described as neither Jew nor Christian but a hanīf who submitted to God, not an associator. This specifies the religious orientation named in the source and distinguishes it from later labels.
terra: لَا خَلَاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ uses khalāq as allotted portion, a specific Qur'anic counter-sense to the lexical value “religion” named in the section.
terra: Seeking a dīn other than God's is confronted with the willing or unwilling submission of everything in heavens and earth and its return to Him; created order and religion coincide.
terra: The intervening profession believes in the revelations to Abraham and the prophets without division, specifying the submission whose exclusive validity 3:85 states.
terra: A dīn other than islām is rejected, and its seeker loses in the Hereafter, setting a firm boundary around religion as submission.

luna: This ayah asks how God would guide people who disbelieved after believing and bearing witness to the Messenger's truth. Its “after their faith” sequence is a close parallel to the source's word بعد and its return-from-faith examples. | terra: The question asks how God would guide people who disbelieved after their faith despite bearing witness and receiving clear proofs, specifying the “after belief” regression.

luna: After the preceding account of people who disbelieved after faith, this ayah makes an exception for those who repent and mend their ways. It parallels the source's distinction between a fall and a faithful, righteous exception. | terra: After disbelief following faith, repentance and أَصْلَحُوا reopen mercy, showing that religious reversal can itself be answered by moral repair.
terra: Disbelieving after faith and then increasing in disbelief is a repeated formulation of the section's regression “after belief,” with repentance no longer credited as sincere.

luna: The ayah commands people to follow Abraham's way as a hanīf. It directly supplies another Quranic formulation of the source's hanīf, upright religion. | terra: The command to follow Abraham's ḥanīf milla gives concrete content to the upright religion named in 6:161.

luna: The source cites the warning that some seek to turn believers into disbelievers “بَعْدَ إِيمَٰنِكُمْ.” This directly joins the root ر د د named in the source to its “after faith” sequence. | terra: يَرُدُّوكُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ كَافِرِينَ places r-d-d, “after,” faith, and unbelief in one warning, as the prose explicitly observes.

luna: The ayah says whoever holds fast to God has been guided to a straight path. It gives a specific means of remaining on the upright course described in the source. | terra: Holding fast to God leads to صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ, expressing the support-and-straight-way relation without the source's exact vocabulary of religion.
terra: Holding together to God's rope and refusing division makes religion a sustaining bond by which a people stands, complementing “establish the dīn and do not divide.”
terra: Darkened faces are asked, “Did you disbelieve after your faith?”, giving the after-faith reversal its judgment-day manifestation.
terra: أُمَّةٌ قَائِمَةٌ describes an upright community whose night recitation and prostration make q-w-m a settled religious disposition.
terra: The upright community believes, commands right, forbids wrong, and hastens in good deeds; this ayah supplies the conduct by which 3:113's standing is known.

luna: After the Prophet's death, the ayah asks whether people would turn back on their heels. It is a specific reversal after faith, though the verse frames it as a question rather than asserting that the believers do so. | terra: أَنْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ and “whoever turns back on his heels” stage religious regression as bodily reversal while affirming that it cannot harm God.

luna: Believers are warned that obeying disbelievers would make them turn back on their heels and become losers. This gives the source's return-to-disbelief image a concrete social pressure and outcome. | terra: Obeying the disbelievers would يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ and turn believers into losers, directly combining external reversal, backward motion, and religious loss.

luna: The source names qiwām as what allows a thing to stand; this ayah calls people's property “قِيَامًا لَّكُمْ,” a means by which their lives are maintained. The link is the dictionary's support-sense, not the ayah's use of “upright religion.” | terra: Wealth is something God made قِيَامًا for people, a concrete Qur'anic instance of the source sense “that by which something stands.”
terra: خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا qualifies “best taqwīm”: good fitted creation does not erase the human constitution's weakness.

luna: The section's dictionary form for qayyim includes a person who manages a people's affairs and sets them right; this ayah uses the related plural “قَوَّامُونَ” for men's responsibility toward women, explaining it through provision and responsibility. The family setting makes the management branch concrete. | terra: قَوَّامُونَ uses q-w-m for sustained care and responsibility within a household, directly illustrating the source dictionary's “one who manages and sets a people right.”

luna: The source's root ر د د dictionary note describes returning oneself to disbelief; this ayah uses the same root to command disputed matters to be referred back to God and the Messenger. The contrasting return shows the root can also name a corrective return to religious authority.
terra: Faith is denied until people accept the Prophet's judgment, feel no inner resistance, and submit fully; this closely explicates īmān as the soul's assent and surrender to truth.

luna: The source names 30:30's “no change in Allah's creation” as part of the fitrah link; Satan here threatens to command people to “فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ ٱللَّهِ” (change Allah's creation). The ayah voices the opposing pressure against the created orientation; the context is Satan's promise, not an endorsement of it. | terra: Satan's command that people فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ directly opposes 30:30's “no alteration in God's creation,” the section's key boundary between given fiṭra and its attempted distortion.

luna: This ayah calls the one who submits his face to God while doing good and follows Abraham's hanīf way the best in religion. The joined face, religion, and good action echo the section's orientation toward upright religion and its faithful deeds. | terra: The best dīn is embodied by one who submits his face to God, does good, and follows Abraham as a ḥanīf; this enacts the section's link between upright religion and righteous conduct.

luna: The source names the ق و م dictionary form “al-qawām” as justice; this ayah commands believers to be “قَوَّامِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ,” standing firmly for justice even against themselves or kin. It shows justice as a practiced form of uprightness. | terra: كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ commands believers to stand persistently for justice even against self and kin, carrying uprightness into moral action.

luna: This ayah describes people believing, disbelieving, believing again, and disbelieving again, then increasing in disbelief. It makes the section's return-from-faith image a repeated pattern, using the different but concrete wording of alternating faith and denial.

luna: If the source's “lowest of the low” is read as an ultimate condemned station, this ayah places hypocrites in the lowest depths of the Fire. That interpretation is not developed in the source section, so the connection is uncertain. | terra: Hypocrites occupy الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ, a moral and eschatological realization of “lowest,” whose exception is supplied in the next ayah.
terra: The exception to the lowest depth is repentance, إصلاح, holding fast to God, and making dīn sincere; they are placed with believers who receive reward, closely matching 95:5-6.
terra: Belief and holding fast to God lead into a straight path, joining inward faith, stable support, and direction.

luna: The source names “al-qawām” as justice; this ayah commands believers to be “قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ” and not let hatred make them unjust. Justice is the upright boundary that holds even under pressure. | terra: كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ ... بِالْقِسْطِ makes standing for God and just witness the conduct nearest to taqwā.
terra: لَا تَرْتَدُّوا عَلَى أَدْبَارِكُمْ uses the r-d-d family for literal retreat from a commanded advance, the bodily image underlying apostasy's backward turn.
terra: Repenting after wrongdoing and doing iṣlāḥ makes moral repair the answer to a fallen course.

luna: The ayah asks who among believers would turn back from their religion, then describes God bringing a people He loves who love Him. It gives both the apostasy sense of the source's r-d-d note and a response to that reversal. | terra: مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ names apostasy directly, then promises that God will bring a faithful people in the apostates' place.

luna: The source's dictionary form “qiwām” means a support by which something stands; this ayah says God made the sacred House “قِيَامًا لِّلنَّاسِ” (a support for people), along with the sacred months and offerings. It gives that secondary support-sense a concrete communal instance. | terra: The Kaaba is made قِيَامًا لِلنَّاسِ, extending q-w-m from bodily uprightness to an institution that sustains communal life.
terra: Whoever does evil in ignorance and afterward repents and reforms receives mercy, pairing “after” with recovery through iṣlāḥ.

luna: Abraham turns his face toward the One who created the heavens and earth as a hanīf, rejecting association. This is a direct scene of orientation to the Creator that parallels the source's fitrah and face-to-religion link. | terra: Abraham directs his face as a ḥanīf to the One who فَطَرَ the heavens and earth, directly joining primordial making, orientation, and monotheistic religion.
terra: Whomever God guides has the breast opened to islām, while misguidance makes it constricted, locating religious direction in the inward human state under divine agency.
luna: God identifies the straight path as His way and says its signs have been detailed. This is a direct repeated formulation of the source's straight-course sense of istiqāma.
terra: Full measure and weight with justice, just speech, and covenant-keeping immediately precede the command to follow God's straight path, embodying upright religion as equitable acts.

luna: God calls this His straight path, commands people to follow it, and warns against other paths that divide them from it. This makes the section's “upright religion” an actual course of conduct with a defined opposite. | terra: هَذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ explicitly turns the upright method into a path one must follow and contrasts it with diverging ways.

luna: The section cites the Prophet being commanded to call his religion “دِينًا قِيَمًا” and Abraham's hanīf way; this ayah states both in its own command. It supplies a concrete prophetic model for the upright religion named by the source's ق و م dictionary form. | terra: The commanded declaration دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا is the section's cited formulation of upright religion.
terra: Prayer, sacrifice, life, and death are declared wholly for God immediately after the announcement of the upright dīn, expanding religion into an entire lived state.
terra: The rejection of partners and command to be first among those who submit completes the stance introduced by dīnan qiyaman in 6:161.
terra: God says He created and shaped humanity before commanding the angels to prostrate to Adam, adding bestowed dignity to the formed-human scene.
terra: أَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ and مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ join upright orientation and sincere obedience with “as He began you, you return,” making creation, religion, and return one movement.

luna: The ayah forbids corruption on earth after it has been set right. It uses the same repair-versus-corruption relationship as the source's ṣ-l-ḥ dictionary definition and connects good deeds to maintaining what is sound. | terra: The command not to corrupt the earth بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا makes fasād a reversal after established ṣalāḥ, closely matching the section's concern with falling away after right formation.

luna: Shuayb commands his people to give full measure and not spread corruption on earth after it has been set right. This joins the source's ṣ-l-ḥ versus fasād distinction to just action in a concrete setting. | terra: Full measure and weight and the ban on corruption after the earth's reform join just ordering with the exact ṣalāḥ/fasād reversal.
terra: Those who hold fast to the Book and أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ are called مُصْلِحِينَ, and God does not waste their reward; adherence, q-w-m, reform, and recompense meet here.

luna: God makes humanity testify that He is their Lord before they enter ordinary life, so they cannot plead ignorance. This gives the source's fitrah claim a specific Quranic scene of an original recognition of God.
terra: A person given God's signs slips out of them and follows Satan, a precise scene of abandoning an already granted direction.
terra: God could have raised him by the signs, but he clings to earth and follows desire; height and self-chosen lowness sharply illuminate the return toward the lowest.

luna: People who fail to use their hearts, eyes, and ears are compared to cattle and said to be even more astray. This is a specific Quranic picture of human capacities falling below their proper use, illuminating the source's descent from the best constitution.
terra: فَمَا اسْتَقَامُوا لَكُمْ فَاسْتَقِيمُوا لَهُمْ applies istiqāma to faithful treaty conduct, a concrete social use of upright human behavior.

luna: “ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ” is the exact upright-religion phrase named in the section; its context then forbids people to wrong themselves in the sacred months. This gives the upright course a concrete ethical boundary. | terra: The ordained measure of sacred months and the command not to wrong oneself are called الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ, giving upright religion a just ordering of conduct and time.
terra: The declaration “you disbelieved after your faith” is another exact religious reversal, here exposed after mockery rather than external coercion.

terra: خَلَاق names the worldly share enjoyed by earlier peoples and their imitators; its “portion” sense differs from the source gloss “religion,” while imitation makes an inherited way of life part of the warning.
terra: The ayah says the offenders disbelieved after their islām, another direct formulation of leaving a previously assumed religious state.
terra: People make dīn sincere to God in danger and then transgress after rescue, showing a temporary religious state rather than the stable disposition the section calls upright.

luna: Moses says that God does not set right the work of corrupters. The ayah applies the source's ṣalāḥ/fasād opposition directly to people's actions, although its scene is Moses confronting sorcery.
terra: Moses and Aaron are told فَاسْتَقِيمَا and not to follow the way of the ignorant, making steadfastness obedience after answered prayer.

luna: Like the source's explanation of the command to turn the face toward religion in 30:30, this command tells the Prophet to set his face toward the religion as a hanīf and not be among the associators. It makes the orientation a committed religious stance. | terra: The command أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا is a close parallel to the section's central command and makes uprightness an active religious stance.
terra: When mercy is removed, the human becomes despairing and ungrateful, beginning a portrait of unstable disposition under changing conditions.
terra: After hardship is replaced by favor, the same human becomes exultant and boastful, showing his state pulled about by circumstance.
terra: The exception is those who remain patient and do righteous deeds, for whom are forgiveness and great reward; this closely parallels 95:6's exception and reward.
terra: Ṣāliḥ commands worship of the God who produced people from the earth and settled them in it, then calls for forgiveness and repentance; origin and religious return meet.
terra: Just measure and weight are commanded together with a ban on depriving people and spreading corruption, making qawām-like justice the opposite of fasād.

luna: The Prophet is told “فَٱسْتَقِمْ كَمَآ أُمِرْتَ” and told that those who repent with him must not transgress. The source names istiqāma as staying with the straight course; this is its direct commanded practice. | terra: فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ commands the Prophet and repentant companions to remain upright and not transgress.

luna: The ayah says the Lord would not destroy towns unjustly while their people were setting things right. It connects righteous conduct with judgment, the two ideas joined in the source's faith, good works, and dīn. | terra: God does not destroy communities unjustly while their people are مُصْلِحُونَ, showing reform as conduct that keeps collective life standing.

luna: The source's dictionary form “al-dīn al-qayyim” is directly echoed by “ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ.” In this ayah the phrase follows the claim that judgment belongs to God alone and that worship is for Him, joining upright religion to divine authority. | terra: Exclusive worship under God's judgment is identified as الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ, defining upright religion as obedience rather than an abstract label.
terra: دِينِ الْمَلِكِ means the king's governing law or order, a Qur'anic instance of dīn as an established way of affairs rather than creed alone.
terra: Joseph addresses the Creator of heavens and earth as his protector and asks to die in submission and join the righteous, joining origination, dīn, ṣalāḥ, and life's end.
terra: Breaking God's covenant after binding it, severing commanded bonds, and spreading corruption show a sustained religious order deliberately undone in action.

luna: The source defines qayyim as one who manages and sets right; this ayah calls God “قَائِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ” (watching over every soul) and its deeds. It is a related overseeing sense, not the source's upright-religion use. | terra: God is قَائِمٌ عَلَى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ, combining q-w-m oversight with each person's deeds and thus approaching the source's governor sense.
terra: The messengers appeal to God as Originator of heavens and earth who calls people for forgiveness, connecting creation with the summons to repent.

luna: God makes believers firm with the firm word in this life and the Hereafter. This is a specific support-and-steadfastness parallel to the source's q-w-m senses of a sustaining foundation and adherence to the straight course. | terra: God makes believers firm with الْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ and leads wrongdoers astray, specifying divine agency in steadfastness and moral displacement.
terra: God's fashioning of the human and breathing into him precede the angels' prostration, a specific image of completed form and honor.
terra: The human is created from a drop and then becomes a manifest disputant; the moral posture sharply reverses the humility implied by his origin.
luna: God says the straight course belongs to Him while some paths deviate. This gives the source's straight religious way a specific contrast between guidance and deviation.

luna: The ayah says worship belongs to God alone and that dīn belongs to Him enduringly. This directly supports the source's dictionary sense of dīn as obedience and an established religious way. | terra: Everything in heavens and earth belongs to God and وَلَهُ الدِّينُ وَاصِبًا describes enduring obedience, bringing dīn close to a permanent state.

luna: If “asfala sāfilīn” in the source also allows the bodily reading of decline in old age, this ayah gives a specific parallel: God creates people, then some reach the most decrepit age and lose knowledge. That reading is not developed in the section, so the connection is uncertain. | terra: اللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ ... وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلَى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ directly joins human creation, divine returning, and the lowest stage of age.

luna: In a parable, one figure commands justice and is on a straight path. This brings together the source's q-w-m dictionary branches of justice and uprightness, with the scene contrasting that person with a helpless dependent. | terra: A powerless dependent is contrasted with one who commands justice and stands on a straight path, linking ability to set affairs right, equity, and upright direction.
terra: Humans leave the womb knowing nothing and receive hearing, sight, and hearts so that they may be grateful, linking created equipment to a religious response.
terra: Whoever acts rightly while believing receives a good life and reward by the best of their deeds, extending the section's faith-and-ṣalāḥ consequence.

luna: This ayah explicitly describes disbelief “after his faith,” while excepting the person compelled whose heart remains secure in faith. It directly echoes the source's post-faith reversal and preserves an important exception in the ayah's own context. | terra: Disbelief after faith is distinguished from coerced speech with a heart secure in faith, sharpening the section's inward definition of īmān and the boundary of apostasy.
terra: Wrongdoing in ignorance followed by repentance and reform is again answered with forgiveness, a repeated route back from corrupted action.

luna: The Prophet is told to follow Abraham's religion as a hanīf, and Abraham is said not to have been among the associators. It gives the section's “upright religion” a concrete inherited model of exclusive devotion. | terra: Revelation commands the Prophet to follow Abraham's milla as a ḥanīf, repeating the prophetic stance behind the section's qiyam dīn.

luna: The Qur'an is said to guide to what is most upright and to give believers who do good deeds news of a great reward. This directly links the source's upright way to the faithful action and reward of 95:6. | terra: The Qur'an guides to الَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ and gives believers who do righteous deeds news of great reward, directly joining the q-w-m superlative, guidance, faith, action, and recompense.
terra: Full measure and weighing with الْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ make straightness a standard of practical justice.

luna: God says He honored the children of Adam, carried them, provided for them, and preferred them over many creatures. This places the source's descent to “the lowest” against an explicit Quranic statement of human dignity. | terra: The children of Adam are honored, carried, provided for, and favored over much creation, a status parallel to best human taqwīm.

luna: The source labels خُلُق as disposition; this ayah says each acts according to “شَاكِلَتِهِ” (his manner or disposition), while God knows best who is guided. It supplies a nonlexical parallel for how a person's settled nature appears in conduct. | terra: “Each acts according to his شَاكِلَتِهِ” states nonlexically that settled formation or disposition takes visible form in action.
terra: The Book has no عِوَجًا, and 18:2 calls it قَيِّمًا; crookedness and uprightness form an explicit boundary in revealed guidance.
terra: The Book is قَيِّمًا so that it warns and gives believers who do righteous deeds news of a good reward, joining upright guidance and the 95:6 response.
terra: مَاكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًا makes the good reward announced with the upright Book in 18:2 explicitly enduring, paralleling ghayr mamnūn.

luna: Moses says God gave each thing its created form and then guided it. This is a specific parallel to the source's link between creation and the direction appropriate to that creation. | terra: “Our Lord is He who gave each thing its created form, then guided it” states the section's core movement from fitted creation to direction.
terra: The magicians refuse to prefer Pharaoh over clear proofs and الَّذِي فَطَرَنَا, making loyalty to the One who formed them govern their religious choice.
terra: The criminal who comes to his Lord has Hell, where he neither dies nor lives, an extreme low destination for a corrupted course.
terra: The one who comes as a believer having done righteous deeds receives the highest degrees, a direct high/low reversal built from the same faith-and-action pair as 95:6.
terra: Everlasting gardens complete the believer's high reward and clarify the enduring side of that contrast.
terra: Forgiveness is promised to one who repents, believes, acts rightly, and then remains guided, gathering the section's inward assent, صالح action, and continued direction.

luna: Whoever turns away from God's remembrance is promised a constricted life and will be raised blind. This specifies a consequence of turning away that illuminates the source's movement from created orientation to a low condition.
terra: خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ gives haste as a created human tendency, a specific boundary on reading best formation as perfected conduct.
terra: The staged making from dust, drop, clot, and womb ends with some being returned to the feeblest age, a detailed creation-and-decline counterpart to 95:4-5.
terra: One who worships God “on an edge” turns his face back when tested and loses both worlds, the opposite of setting the face firmly to upright religion.
terra: God's repelling of some people by others prevents monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques from being demolished, showing divine support keeping worship standing in the world.
terra: Those established in the land establish prayer, give alms, command right, and forbid wrong, showing q-w-m authority used to rectify communal conduct.
terra: Striving, the religion without constriction, Abraham's milla, being named Muslims, prayer, charity, and holding fast to God make dīn a sustaining whole.
terra: Creating the human from an extract of clay supplies the first material stage of the excellent formation completed in 23:14.
terra: Placement as a drop in a secure resting place supplies the next stage and the protected setting of human formation.

luna: After recounting the stages of human development, this ayah says the human is brought forth as another creation. That formed human is a specific creation parallel to the source's “best taqwīm,” though it does not itself state the moral direction. | terra: The embryo is successively formed and then produced as another creation, ending with praise of the best of creators; it concretizes excellent human formation.
terra: Death follows the detailed formation of 23:12-14, marking the created body's downward boundary.
terra: Resurrection after death completes the formation-to-return sequence and brings the human before judgment.

luna: The ayah rejects the idea that humans were created without purpose or would not be returned to God. It joins creation directly to return and accountability, clarifying why the source moves from human formation to dīn. | terra: “Did you think We created you aimlessly and that you would not be returned?” directly makes created purpose entail return and accountability.

luna: When believers are called to God and the Messenger for judgment, their answer is that they hear and obey. This gives a concrete instance of the source's dīn-as-obedience sense; the call to judgment is stated in 24:48–50. | terra: True believers answer God's judgment with “we hear and obey,” a direct behavioral expression of faith as assent and dīn as obedience.
luna: Those who refuse guidance are likened to cattle, or further astray, and called heedless. This sharpens the source's contrast between the formed human and the low state that follows rejection.
terra: Measured spending between extravagance and stinginess is قَوَامًا, directly exemplifying the source dictionary's qawām as just balance.

luna: The source labels خُلُق as an innate habit or disposition; this ayah uses “خُلُقُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ” for the way of earlier peoples (often rendered their custom). That secondary customary sense links a settled way of life with the section's neighboring dictionary sense of dīn as habit or condition. | terra: خُلُقُ الْأَوَّلِينَ denotes the habitual way of former peoples, a Qur'anic use of the khalq family in precisely the character/custom field developed in the prose.
terra: The powerful offenders يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ, an exact Qur'anic pairing of corruption with failure to act rightly.
terra: Giving full measure and refusing to cause loss opens a three-ayah picture of upright commercial conduct.
terra: Weighing with the straight balance explicitly joins istiqāma and justice.
terra: Not diminishing people's goods and not roaming as corrupters supplies the fasād boundary of the preceding straight measure.
terra: The people are told to fear the One who created them and former generations, grounding taqwā in created dependence.
terra: Doing good as God has done good is opposed to seeking corruption on earth, locating ṣalāḥ's contrary in chosen action.

terra: People “fabricate falsehood” and worship powerless idols, whereas provision, worship, gratitude, and return belong to God; the khalq root's fabrication sense is set against divine origination and true dīn.
terra: Traveling the earth to see how creation began is made evidence that God will produce the later creation, linking origin to accountability.
terra: Shipwreck fear produces sincere dīn, but deliverance produces renewed association; the scene dramatizes failure to remain on the confessed direction.
terra: Heaven and earth تَقُومَانِ بِأَمْرِهِ, showing the created cosmos held standing by divine command before humans are called forth.

luna: The section joins the source roots خ ل ق and ق و م in human creation and upright religion; this ayah joins Allah's creation of people on fitrah, the command to turn one's face toward religion, and dīn al-qayyim. Its “no change in Allah's creation” makes the claimed fitrah-religion alignment explicit. | terra: This is the section's explicit Qur'anic meeting: setting the face to dīn, God-given fiṭra, unaltered khalq, and الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ bind formed nature to upright religion.
terra: Turning penitently to God, taqwā, prayer, and refusal of shirk specify the conduct of the fiṭra and upright dīn named in 30:30.
terra: Corruption appears through what people's hands have earned so that they taste consequences and perhaps return; conduct deforms order and is meant to prompt reversal.

luna: The section says a person's istiqāma is staying with the straight course; here the command is to set one's face toward the upright religion before a day that cannot be turned away. It joins the source's orientation image to steadfast practice and judgment. | terra: أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ الْقَيِّمِ repeats the face-and-upright-dīn scene and adds the deadline of the unavoidable Day.
terra: After the command to set the face to upright religion, disbelief is charged to the disbeliever while righteous action is something people prepare for themselves.
terra: God's rewarding of believers who do righteous deeds completes the consequence of standing toward the upright religion in 30:43.

luna: If the source's descent to “asfala sāfilīn” includes bodily decline, this ayah's human arc from weakness to strength and back to weakness is a concrete parallel. The section itself emphasizes religious direction, so this reading remains uncertain. | terra: God creates from weakness, gives strength, then after strength appoints weakness and grey age; the rise and reversal spell out the human arc compressed in 95:4-5.
terra: One who يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ while doing good has grasped the firmest handle, picturing upright religion as submission and stable support.
terra: Calling God with sincere dīn in enveloping waves is followed by divided responses on land, with only some remaining measured and steadfast.
terra: أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ says God made everything He created good and immediately begins the creation of the human, closely echoing best-created form.

luna: After creation from clay and the human lineage, God fashions the person, breathes of His spirit, and gives hearing, sight, and hearts, yet few are grateful. It connects formed human capacities with the moral response central to the source's shift from creation to faith and deeds. | terra: After God fashions the human and gives hearing, sight, and hearts, “little are you grateful” makes moral response the test of fitted form.
terra: A believing man or woman has no contrary choice once God and His Messenger decide; disobedience is manifest straying, so faith is defined through submission.
terra: The speaker asks why he should not worship the One who فَطَرَنِي and to whom all return, making origination the reason for dīn.
luna: God says He commanded the children of Adam not to worship Satan but to worship Him, “this is a straight path.” The verse joins obedience to the source's straight-course image.
terra: وَمَنْ نُعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّسْهُ فِي الْخَلْقِ states the physical reversal of created form that the section's return to the lowest can carry.

luna: The ayah asks whether a human does not see that God created him from a drop, yet he becomes a clear opponent. It is a specific creation-to-denial parallel to the source's movement from human formation to denial of dīn. | terra: The human created from a drop becomes a manifest opponent, a sharp creation-to-denial reversal resembling the section's movement from formation to denying dīn.

luna: The human who disputes resurrection forgets his own creation and asks who will revive decayed bones. This supplies the challenge that 36:79 answers, paralleling the source's movement from creation to a question of judgment. | terra: The opponent forgets his own creation while challenging resurrection, specifying the failure of inference that the section's rhetorical question exposes.

luna: The answer is that the One who produced the bones the first time will revive them. It completes 36:78 and directly joins original creation to return, clarifying the accountability behind dīn. | terra: The answer appeals to the One who created the first time, making original creation the proof of return and judgment.
luna: The resurrected say this is the Day of Judgment. It directly activates dīn as reckoning in a scene of resurrection and accountability.
luna: This identifies the Day of Separation and says it is the day people denied, completing 37:20's Day of Judgment. It directly links the source's denial question to its judgment sense.
terra: Worshipping God مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينَ defines dīn as sincere obedience in a direct command.
terra: “The pure dīn belongs to God” distinguishes sincere obedience from the patronage offered to intermediaries.
terra: One who is devout through the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy, embodies a settled religious state in literal posture.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to worship God sincerely in dīn. This makes the source's dictionary sense of dīn as obedience concrete as exclusive worship. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to worship God while making dīn sincere, reinforcing religion as an enacted submission.

luna: The Prophet says he worships God, making his religion sincere for Him alone. It is a direct lived instance of the source's dīn-as-obedience sense. | terra: The Prophet is told to worship God while making his dīn sincere, repeating religion as a personally enacted submission.
terra: A breast opened to islām and light from God is contrasted with hardened hearts, another precise link between dīn and settled inner disposition.
terra: The Qur'an is Arabic غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ, “without crookedness,” a direct negative boundary around the upright revealed way.
terra: Calling upon God with dīn made sincere, even against unbelievers' dislike, presents obedience as an undivided stance.
terra: Pharaoh fears Moses will change “your dīn” or cause corruption, exposing dīn as an established public order while inverting who actually embodies fasād.
terra: Male or female believers who act rightly enter the Garden and receive provision without reckoning, a close reward parallel to 95:6.

luna: This ayah says God fashioned people and made their forms good, after making the earth a dwelling and the sky a canopy. It is a direct parallel to the source's formed human, though it does not itself develop the later moral reversal. | terra: وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ explicitly says God formed humans and made their forms good, then calls them to the Lord of the worlds.
terra: The living God alone is invoked with sincere dīn, grounding enduring obedience in the One who does not die.
terra: The human's creation through successive stages to maturity and old age expands the bodily arc between formation and decline.
terra: فَاسْتَقِيمُوا إِلَيْهِ commands a straight course toward the one God, closely realizing the section's definition of human istiqāma as adhering to the upright way.
terra: Withholding alms and denying the Hereafter supply the contrary conduct between the command to be straight in 41:6 and the unending reward in 41:8.

luna: Those who believe and do righteous deeds are promised “أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ,” the same uncut reward named in the source's 95:6. It confirms the reward as a repeated Quranic promise to this group. | terra: Belief and righteous deeds receive أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, the exact reward formula of 95:6 within a passage that has just commanded istiqāma.

luna: Those who say their Lord is God and then remain upright receive the angels' reassurance. This gives the source's istikāma (adherence to the straight course) a specific form: steadfastness after professing faith. | terra: Those who say “our Lord is God” and then اسْتَقَامُوا embody settled confession carried into continued uprightness.

luna: This ayah says the same religion was enjoined on Noah, Muhammad, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, and commands “أَنْ أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ” (establish the religion). It makes the section's upright religion a continuous prophetic way rather than a merely personal disposition. | terra: أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ turns the q-w-m family into a command to uphold one religion without division.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to invite, remain upright as commanded, not follow people's desires, and “أُمِرْتُ لِأَعْدِلَ بَيْنَكُم” (be just among you). It brings together the section's straight course, obedience, and q-w-m dictionary branch of justice. | terra: فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ makes prophetic uprightness obedience to command and couples it with belief in revelation and equitable judgment.
luna: Revelation is described as a light by which God guides to a straight path. It makes the source's upright religious direction concrete as revealed guidance.
terra: Abraham rejects inherited objects of worship except الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي, trusting that his Maker will guide him; formation and direction meet in a polemic against custom.

luna: The Prophet is told to hold fast to what is revealed because he is on a straight path. The revealed guidance here makes concrete the upright religious direction the source traces from human creation. | terra: Holding fast to revelation is warranted because the addressee is عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ, linking adherence to the upright path.
luna: The ayah says whoever does good does so for himself and whoever does evil does so against himself, then all return to God. It connects the source's righteous deeds to an individual reckoning.
terra: God created heavens and earth in truth so that every soul may be repaid for what it earned; creation, just measure, and judgment form one claim.

luna: The ayah describes someone who makes desire his god, then has hearing and heart sealed and sight covered. It is a particular way the created human capacities can be turned from their intended guidance, matching the source's moral descent.
luna: The ayah says God gives life and death and will gather people on the Day of Resurrection, of which there is no doubt. It directly joins creation and human life to the judgment-sense of dīn.
terra: The same confession followed by اسْتَقَامُوا brings freedom from fear and grief, emphasizing permanence in the religious course.

luna: Those who believe and do righteous deeds are said to have their misdeeds removed and their condition set right. This links the source's faith and ṣāliḥ deeds to God's setting the believers right. | terra: Those who believe, act righteously, and affirm the revealed truth have their evils removed and their state أَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ; God actively rectifies the believing people.
terra: Supporting God's cause brings divine support and firm feet, a concrete image of religion as that by which believers remain standing.
terra: Turning away is pictured as spreading corruption and severing kinship, making religious retreat visible in anti-ṣalāḥ acts.

luna: This ayah describes people who turn back after guidance has become clear, with Satan making it seem easy to them. It directly parallels the source's movement from upright guidance toward return and denial. | terra: Those who ارْتَدُّوا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهِمْ after guidance became clear embody a backward movement away from an already disclosed straight course.
terra: The distinction between merely saying “we believe” and faith entering the hearts sharpens the section's definition of īmān as inward assent, while obedience is named as its operative test.
terra: True believers are those whose faith is not followed by doubt and whose striving proves it, sharpening faith as settled assent expressed in acts.
terra: God's lack of weariness in the first creation exposes human doubt about a new creation, another creation-to-return argument.

luna: The ayah swears that “إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ لَوَاقِعٌ” (the Judgment will surely occur). This directly activates the judgment sense of dīn that can be heard in the source's question after creation and moral action.
terra: The creation of jinn and humans is given the purpose of worship, directly placing created being on the line of religious obedience.
terra: God raises the heaven and sets the balance, presenting upright created order as measured equilibrium.
terra: The prohibition against transgressing the balance turns cosmic measure into a boundary for human behavior.
terra: أَقِيمُوا الْوَزْنَ بِالْقِسْطِ commands people to establish weight justly, joining q-w-m, measure, and justice in action.
terra: Revelation and the balance are sent لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ: religion makes people stand in justice, almost a Qur'anic enactment of the source dictionary's qiwām and upright conduct.
terra: When the people deviate, God causes their hearts to deviate; this reverses istiqāma and highlights the divine agency also present in “We returned him.”

luna: God created people, yet some disbelieve and some believe. This directly places the section's created human and subsequent faith or denial on the same axis; creation does not erase the moral divergence.

luna: God creates the heavens and earth, fashions people beautifully, and says the return is to Him. It joins the source's beautifully ordered human creation to accountability. | terra: خَلَقَ ... وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ joins creation in truth, beautiful human form, and final destination.
terra: The creation of death and life is for testing أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا, placing “best” created order in direct relation to the quality of deeds.
terra: God produces humans and gives hearing, sight, and hearts, yet they give little thanks; fitted faculties and failed disposition stand together.
terra: أَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ exactly repeats the unending-reward phrase and directly precedes the Qur'an's description of the Prophet's khuluq.

luna: The source labels the dictionary form خُلُق as innate disposition or character; this ayah calls the Prophet's character “خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ.” It makes the section's move from created nature to an established moral disposition concrete. | terra: خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ uses the source section's khalq-family sense “inborn character”; beside 68:3 it joins character to the same unending reward as 95:6.
terra: إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا names an anxious created disposition, directly activating the prose's khalq/khuluq relation between constitution and character.
terra: Distress makes that created anxious person panic, specifying how the disposition of 70:19 appears in conduct.
terra: Good fortune makes that person withholding, completing the behavioral portrait before the exception for worshippers.
terra: إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ interrupts the general human disposition with a religious exception, structurally paralleling 95:6's exception for believers who act rightly.
terra: The worshippers excepted from anxious human disposition are constant in prayer, making steadiness itself the distinguishing religious habit.
terra: Those formed by the intervening faithful practices are honored in gardens, supplying the endpoint opposite anxious and withholding conduct.
terra: “He created you in stages” states ordered human formation in compact form.
terra: God causing humans to grow from the earth like a growth gives organic form to created constitution.
terra: God then returns people to the earth and brings them forth again, completing formation with divinely governed return.
terra: Remaining straight عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ is answered with abundant provision, a direct instance of istiqāma as staying on the established way.
terra: The condemned say they were not among those who prayed, beginning a conduct-based explanation that culminates in denial of the Day of dīn.
terra: They did not feed the poor, pairing failed worship with failed social action as in the behavioral exposure of dīn-denial.
terra: They joined vain or wrongful discourse with those who indulged in it, showing a habitual social course.

luna: The speakers say they used to deny the Day of Judgment. This is a direct denial formulation for the judgment-sense of dīn that can be heard in the source's closing question. | terra: “We used to deny the Day of dīn” names the belief that corresponds to the preceding corrupt practices.
terra: Their pattern continued until certainty came, emphasizing persistence in the denying disposition rather than a momentary lapse.

luna: The ayah asks whether a human thinks he will be left without responsibility, then 75:37–40 recount origin and formation and God's power to resurrect. It makes created human form answerable to the coming judgment. | terra: The question whether the human expects to be left purposeless opens a creation argument for accountability.

luna: This names the human's origin as a drop, beginning 75:37–40's argument that the One who formed him can resurrect him. It gives a concrete creation-to-accountability parallel to the source's sequence. | terra: The human's origin as an emitted drop supplies the first stage of that accountability argument.

luna: This says the drop became a clinging form and was then proportioned; 75:37 and 75:39–40 complete the creation-to-resurrection argument. The formed body links to the source's human constitution. | terra: ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى makes creation and proportioning the decisive middle of the argument.

luna: This says God made the human pair male and female, completing the account of formation that grounds 75:40's resurrection question. It supplies another specific part of human creation behind accountability. | terra: Making the human pair male and female displays the completed created order under discussion.

luna: The surah concludes its account of human origin and formation by asking whether the Creator cannot bring the dead to life. It joins creation to the judgment and return implied by the source's dīn. | terra: The closing question infers God's power to revive the dead from the fitted creation just recounted, paralleling the move from creation to dīn as judgment.
terra: God creates the human from a mixed drop as a test and equips him with hearing and sight, joining formation and moral purpose.
terra: After created equipment, God guides the way and the human becomes grateful or ungrateful; this states the movement from fit creation to chosen stance.
terra: The revelation is a reminder, so whoever wills may take a way to the Lord; this continues the created-and-guided human scene of 76:2-3.
terra: Human willing is placed within God's will, clarifying the divine agency behind taking or leaving the directed way.

luna: The one who transgresses is set at the head of a passage ending in Hell for those who prefer worldly life (79:38–39). This gives a specific moral route toward ruin that contrasts with the faithful exception in the source.

luna: This ayah specifies the preference for worldly life as the transgressor's orientation; 79:37 names the transgression and 79:39 its Hell consequence. It offers a concrete contrary direction to the source's upright faith and righteous work.

luna: Hell is the destination completing 79:37–38's transgression and preference for worldly life. It gives the downward outcome in that passage separately from the source's promised uncut reward for the faithful.

luna: The contrasting person fears standing before the Lord and restrains the self from desire. This is a concrete inner discipline that leads away from the downward route and complements the section's faith and righteous acts.
luna: Paradise is the destination completing 79:40's restraint of desire, in contrast with 79:37–39. It gives a specific lasting outcome for a person whose conduct stays oriented to God.
terra: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ joins creation and measured fitting in the human body.
terra: ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ follows measured creation with an eased way, making bodily formation and directed course consecutive.
terra: The question “what deceived you concerning your generous Lord?” opens the creation-to-denial sequence and parallels the section's challenge “what then makes you deny?”

luna: The source names taqwīm as an upright, well-set human constitution; here God says He created the person, then “فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ” (proportioned and balanced you). The neighboring 82:8 completes the act by saying He assembled the person in whatever form He willed. | terra: خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ is the closest creation scene: God creates, proportionally forms, and balances the human before the passage names denial of dīn.

luna: This ayah completes 82:7's creation and balancing: “فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ” says God composed the human in the form He willed. It specifies the formed human behind the section's “best taqwīm.” | terra: God composes the human in whatever form He wills, completing 82:7's shaping before 82:9's accusation of denying dīn.

luna: The section explicitly connects its account of creation and moral direction to this next claim in the same surah: “بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ.” Here denial of dīn follows the forming in 82:7–8, matching the section's movement from upright creation to denial. | terra: كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ completes 82:7-8's formed-human scene with the same denial of dīn that closes this section.
terra: Guardians placed over people follow the accusation of denying dīn and begin the passage's account of how conduct is preserved for judgment.
terra: The guardians are noble recording scribes, making deeds rather than profession alone the evidence relevant to dīn.
terra: The recorders know what people do, completing the bridge from formed creation and denial to accountable action.
terra: The righteous are in bliss, giving ṣalāḥ its judgment-side outcome after 82:9's denial of dīn.
terra: The wicked are in the Blaze, the contrary outcome paired with 82:13's righteous.
luna: After 82:9's denial of dīn, this ayah says the wicked enter the Fire on the Day of Judgment. It supplies the consequence in the same surah; 82:16 adds that they will not be absent from it.
luna: This completes 82:15 by saying the wicked will not be absent from the Fire on the Day of Judgment. It makes the judgment denied in 82:9 an unavoidable outcome.

luna: The ayah asks what will make people know the Day of Judgment, after 82:15–16 have named its Fire and permanence. It explicitly repeats the dīn of 82:9 as a coming reckoning. | terra: The question “what will make you know what the Day of dīn is?” fixes judgment or recompense as the immediate contextual sense of dīn in 82:9, a vital boundary beside the section's religion reading.

luna: This repeats the question about the Day of Judgment and heightens the warning begun in 82:17. The sequence makes the denied dīn from 82:9 concrete as an approaching event. | terra: Repeating the question intensifies the identification of dīn with the coming Day rather than merely a present communal religion.

luna: The ayah explains that on the Day of Judgment no soul can help another and all command belongs to God. It completes the same surah's warning against denying dīn in 82:9 with the judgment's actual condition. | terra: On that Day no soul controls anything for another and command belongs to God, supplying the content of dīn as final judgment.

luna: This ayah describes people who deny “بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ.” It is a direct Qur'anic formulation of the judgment-sense of dīn that the section's final question can carry. | terra: الَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ repeats denial of dīn explicitly as denial of Judgment Day.

luna: After naming deniers of the Day of Judgment in 83:11, this ayah specifies that the denier is every transgressing sinner. It links rejection of dīn to a concrete moral condition. | terra: Only every transgressing sinner denies that Day, tying denial to a settled moral condition.

luna: This says that when the revelations are recited to the deniers, they call them tales of earlier people. It adds the deniers' response to the judgment-denial named in 83:11. | terra: Calling recited signs “legends of the ancients” gives the denier's stance and speech concrete form.

luna: The ayah says what people have earned has covered their hearts. In the surrounding passage about denying the Day of Judgment, it makes conduct a cause of spiritual obscuration, complementing the source's faith-and-deeds distinction. | terra: What people repeatedly earned has rusted over their hearts, a vivid account of actions becoming an inward disposition.
luna: This says the deniers will be screened from their Lord on that day. It gives a consequence completing the judgment passage that begins by naming denial of the Day of Judgment in 83:11.

luna: This ayah repeats the source's exception almost word for word: those who believe and do righteous deeds have “أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ.” It specifies that the reward is not cut off, exactly clarifying the phrase in 95:6. | terra: The full exception “those who believe and do righteous deeds” and أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ exactly reproduce 95:6 after a scene of denial.

luna: God creates and proportionately forms all things; for the human image, 87:2 continues in 87:3 with measuring and guiding. This is a close parallel to the source's paired ideas of human creation and taqwīm. | terra: الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى presents creation as proportioning and fitting, a close parallel to “the best taqwīm.”

luna: This completes 87:2's created and proportioned order: God measures and guides. It connects formed nature to direction, the same link the source draws between fitrah and dīn al-qayyim. | terra: وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَى continues fitted creation with measure and guidance, the same creation-to-direction relation developed in the prose.
terra: Success belongs to the one who purifies himself, a direct moral response to the created-and-guided human scene earlier in the surah.
terra: Remembering the Lord's name and praying turns purification into concrete religious conduct.

luna: This ayah says people prefer the nearer worldly life; the next says the Hereafter is better and more enduring. That preference supplies a concrete contrary orientation to the enduring reward promised to the faithful in the source. | terra: Preferring the nearer life is the contrary orientation, explaining how a guided creature chooses the lower horizon.

luna: The Hereafter is “خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ” (better and more lasting), completing 87:16's preference for worldly life. This directly clarifies the lasting side of the source's “uninterrupted” reward. | terra: The Hereafter is better and more lasting, setting enduring recompense against the preference in 87:16 and illuminating “unending reward.”
terra: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي كَبَدٍ places human creation in toil, a bodily-life boundary to the claim of best taqwīm.
terra: The gift of two eyes begins a bodily-endowment argument that turns immediately toward moral direction.
terra: A tongue and two lips continue the inventory of fitted human capacities.
terra: Guidance to the two heights or paths converts created faculties into moral alternatives.
terra: The human nevertheless does not cross the steep path, showing failure to use the given formation in its right direction.
terra: The steep path culminates in being among believers who counsel patience and mercy, supplying the faith-and-conduct side of the scene.

luna: God swears by the soul and the One who proportioned it. The source's “best taqwīm” is a well-formed human constitution; this ayah makes the soul's formation the starting point of moral direction. | terra: The oath by the soul and the One who proportioned it makes moral life rest upon a divinely fitted human self.

luna: The formed soul is made to know its wickedness and its piety. This gives a moral counterpart to the source's claim that created human nature is oriented toward the straight religion, while keeping both possible directions in view. | terra: The fitted soul is inspired with both its corruption and its taqwā, locating the moral fork inside the creation scene of 91:7.

luna: The soul succeeds through its purification. This makes the source's exception for those who believe and do righteous deeds (95:6) a specific act of moral cultivation. | terra: Success belongs to one who purifies that divinely formed soul, showing created capacity carried into upright action.

luna: The soul fails when it is buried or corrupted. This is a direct moral reversal of 91:9's purification and illuminates the section's descent from upright constitution to a lower condition. | terra: Failure belongs to one who buries or corrupts that soul, the specific reversal of preserving its given moral direction.
terra: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى announces divergent human courses, opening a compact scene of opposed dispositions and divinely eased destinations.
terra: Giving and guarding oneself supply the first acts of the upright course in 92:4-7.
terra: Affirming “the best” adds inward assent to that course, closely pairing conviction with conduct.
terra: God's “We shall ease him toward ease” makes divine direction answer the person's faith-shaped conduct.
terra: Stinginess and imagined self-sufficiency begin the contrary disposition, reversing giving and taqwā.
terra: Denying “the best” supplies the unbelieving counterpart to 92:6's assent.
terra: God's “We shall ease him toward hardship” is a striking parallel to divine return toward the lowest after the human chooses denial.
terra: اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ makes the Creator the ground of the first command addressed to the Prophet.
terra: خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ identifies the human creation at the start of a passage that soon exposes human transgression.
terra: كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى turns from created-and-taught humanity to its moral descent, a close structural reversal of fitted creation.
terra: The human transgresses because he sees himself self-sufficient, naming the disposition behind the fall.
terra: إِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الرُّجْعَى answers self-sufficiency with inevitable return, restoring the Creator's authority over human direction.

luna: The section specifically points to this ending, “وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ ٱلْقَيِّمَةِ.” The ayah describes sincere worship, prayer, and zakah as what they were commanded, so upright religion appears as lived obedience. | terra: Worship with sincere dīn, prayer, and almsgiving are gathered under دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ, so upright religion becomes a pattern of acts.

luna: The neighboring 98:7 calls believers with righteous deeds “خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ”; this ayah calls the disbelievers among the People of the Book and polytheists “شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ.” The paired ranking makes the section's fall and its faithful exception concrete; this row states the negative side.

luna: This ayah calls those who believe and do righteous deeds “خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ,” while the preceding 98:6 names disbelievers “شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ.” It directly parallels 95:6's exception of faithful doers from the low condition.

luna: This completes 98:7's description of the faithful as the best of creatures by naming their reward: gardens of lasting residence and God's approval. It parallels the source's believers' uncut reward.
terra: The universal statement that the human is in loss provides a moral descent corresponding to the return to the lowest.
terra: The exception for those who believe, do righteous deeds, and sustain truth and patience closely parallels the rescuing exception of 95:6.

luna: The denier of dīn is identified by what follows: repelling the orphan and failing to urge the feeding of the poor (107:2–3). This links dīn as judgment or religion to the ethical conduct the section associates with righteous works. | terra: أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ turns denial of dīn into a question whose answer is displayed in habitual conduct.

luna: The denier of dīn is identified in the next ayah as one who repels the orphan. This gives the source's link between religion and righteous action a concrete social example; 107:1 names the denial itself. | terra: Repelling the orphan is the first concrete act by which 107:1's denial of dīn is recognized, supporting the section's link between religion and character.

luna: The denier of dīn is also one who does not urge feeding the poor. This gives the source's dīn-as-lived-obedience and righteous-deeds themes a concrete social example; 107:1 names the denial itself. | terra: Failure to urge feeding the poor gives denial of dīn a second social and habitual expression.
terra: The warning to worshippers begins a boundary between the outward religious act and the upright disposition the act should embody.
terra: Heedlessness toward prayer shows a religious practice severed from settled obedience.
terra: Showing off makes the religious act serve social display rather than sincere dīn.
terra: Withholding even small aid completes the surah's demonstration that denial of dīn is disclosed by corrupted conduct.
terra: “To you your dīn and to me mine” marks a firm boundary between established religious ways after repeated refusal to exchange worship.
